observedFailure.source: Field reports #11 and #12 against the user's own data root on 2026-09-09, not an observation of these gates.
sequence: 14:03:52Z — a SessionStart maintenance wake handed the extractor model budget fe4a61c1, whose deadline_at had already passed. claimExtractionTarget claimed both pending targets first, incrementing attempts to 1, and the budget was only resolved later inside the model call.

reserveModelAttempt raised deadline exhaustion before inserting any model_work_attempts row, so no provider call was ever made, yet deferMemoryJobForModelBudget parked both jobs with available_at = now + 60min, observed in the database as available_at 15:03:52Z.
14:04:18Z — the same wake minted a fresh budget 26 seconds later, but every job it could have run was already in backoff, so its window expired unused.

14:23Z — a foreground `memex backfill extract` could not claim either job and reported HANDOFF (다른 러너가 처리 중), although lease_owner was NULL and no worker process existed. The operator was shown a phantom runner instead of a retry backoff.

fix.#12: findExhaustedModelBudgetForClaim resolves the job's durable budget before the claim and applies the same exhaustion predicate reserveModelAttempt uses, so a dead budget never costs an attempt; the pre-flight creates nothing, so an unbound job keeps its lazy-creation path. Because the pre-flight and the reservation are still separated by wall clock, deferMemoryJobForModelBudget takes an opt-in claimedAt: a deadline or window stop that follows a claim which reserved no provider attempt refunds that attempt and returns the job to pending at now. An attempts exhaustion keeps the old one-hour fence, because that budget really was spent.
fix.#11: claimMemoryJobById now reports which of its four refusal reasons applied — lease_held, backoff with the instant it becomes due, attempts_exhausted, cas — from the row the predicate already reads, with no extra query, no extra write and no change to what is claimable. CLAIM_REJECTION_REPORT is the single source for label, note, bucket and escalation, so the worker cannot print a label that disagrees with its own counters. The worker prints HANDOFF (lease held by another runner), DEFERRED (retry backoff until <ISO>) or SKIPPED (attempt cap reached), counts them as handoff / backoff-deferred / attempt-cap, and escalates only the attempt cap. `memex status` gains a matching backoff breakdown of pending plus the earliest retry time.

backfillScheduling.exitCodeContract: Unchanged. Backoff work stays inside the extract stage's pending count, so `memex backfill extract` still exits 2 for "completed with deferred work"; 0 and 1 keep their meanings and terminal `deferred` keeps its own.
backfillScheduling.regressions: test/model-budget-stale-claim.test.ts (3 cases: a stale budget refuses the claim instead of spending an attempt and an hour of backoff, the fresh budget from the same wake claims the work immediately, and an unspent claim is refunded on a deadline stop while the attempts fence holds); test/claim-rejection-reason.test.ts (5 cases: backoff reported with its due time rather than a phantom runner, a live lease still reported as a handoff, an exhausted attempt cap reported as its own reason, the reason surfaced through runFactExtraction for the worker, and status counting backoff sessions with the earliest retry); test/backfill-cli-slice.test.mjs (1 added case reproducing the exact observed state — lease_owner NULL, no runner, future available_at — and pinning exit 2 with a deferred, not handoff, message). test/backfill-worker-execution.test.ts (10 cases) and test/worker-dist-contract.test.ts (9 cases) cover worker execution and the dist contract, including a dist predating claimReason falling back to the previous HANDOFF behaviour.

releaseConclusion: All thirteen gates PASS on the clean v0.5.1 candidate 3dbf6ed0, each on its first attempt: typecheck, a build that reproduced the tracked dist/, 100 files / 1026 Vitest tests, 26 Codex slices, 106 total slices, installer, marketplace, packaged runtime (memex-0.5.1.tgz, 311 files, 9 MCP tools), offline lifecycle 9/9, the real-Chrome Memex Workspace E2E (10 check groups, 0 runtime errors), 82 Workspace unit tests and the benchmark contract. Isolated plugin validation passes all 11 substitute checks with matching 0.5.1 plugin and MCP server versions, and is PASS-WITH-NOTES only because the formal `codex plugin validate` subcommand does not exist in codex-cli 0.153.4. The release itself is two scheduling fixes: a model budget is now resolved before a job is claimed, so a dead budget no longer burns an attempt and an hour of backoff, and a refused claim now reports whether it was a lease handoff, a retry backoff with its due time, or an exhausted attempt cap, instead of always printing HANDOFF. Nineteen isolated regression cases across model-budget-stale-claim, claim-rejection-reason and the backfill CLI slice reconstruct the observed #11/#12 state and pin the unchanged exit-code contract. No UI code changed, and the Workspace readback assertion held again. The full acceptance benchmark was NOT re-run: it is referenced as prior evidence measured on 236d7362, and no AC_PERF check exercises job claiming, budget resolution or backfill CLI output. The v0.5.0 receipt is archived byte-for-byte as merge-gate-pre-0.5.1.json. Replaying the failing wake against the user's real data root, draining the live backlog, live user data, an authenticated Codex tier run, the formal plugin validator, benchmark numbers for this exact SHA, real-world performance and model quality are NOT_PROVEN.
